Theme 038 · Light, optics & texture

Noir

Hard key light, no fill, venetian-blind shadows slicing across a desk of case files, grain and gate weave from 1940s film. Acme Pulse is the tireless detective reading every file overnight; the only colour allowed is coral, drawn around the clue. At dawn the blinds open and the film ends in daylight and brand colour.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Blind gobo — skewed repeating-linear-gradient stripes; the signature light pattern, adjustable per scene.
  • Hard spotlight — radial mask with no fill light; decides what the viewer is allowed to see.
  • Case files — stacked folders typed "DASHBOARD 38 — UNREAD"; the pain as a physical pile.
  • Frosted door — backlit glass lettering with the Acme mark; the reveal as a detective agency.
  • Evidence board — exhibits, cleared suspects, pins and a coral string; the only colour is the clue.
  • Typed memo — "Your call, boss." with Roll back / Acknowledge; the human decision.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Blind tilt — stripes rotate 4° and change thickness as the blinds are adjusted, power1.inOut 1.5 s, starting on bar downbeats.
  • Light swing — hanging-lamp spotlight sways ±6° on a 3 s sine (1.5 bars at 120 BPM), so light and music breathe together.
  • Gate weave — whole-frame 0.5 px jitter from a seeded table plus grain stepped at 24 fps; never Math.random.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

A detective who reads every file overnight is a warm, human way to describe a background agent, and "only the clue is in colour" makes the anomaly impossible to miss. Risk: noir implies crime and fraud; frame it as a mistake hunt, never wrongdoing, and end in bright daylight.

Adapt to your product: Pin your own screens as exhibits, grey out what your product clears, and draw the coral string from the finding to its root cause.
